newsitem.title: USA: US W.Coast gasolines ease with supply, thin trade.
newsitem.headline: US W.Coast gasolines ease with supply, thin trade.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot unleaded gasoline markets eased midday Monday, as ample supply and little buying interest forced sellers to drop offers, traders said.
Trade began quietly, as refiners figured out their needs after a social function kept many out of markets last week.
"It's just offfers and no buyers," one broker said. "I think the market is undervalued."
West Coast markets are normally quiet Mondays because players want to see weekly inventory data, issued the following evening by the American Petroleum Institute (API).
Last week, the Washington, D.C.-based trade group reported higher West Coast gasoline supplies, with stocks up 1.4 million barrels to 28.1 million.

Outside markets were weak, or rose slightly Monday, with "racks" falling about 1.50 cents a gallon in Los Angeles, and unleaded gasoline futures shading higher by a paltry 0.02 cents, to settle 60.54 cents a gallon.
L.A. spot CARB grade gasoline eased 0.50 cents to 64/65 cents a gallon, while conventional stood half a cent lower at 61/62 cents Monday, traders said.
Distillates held Friday's levels after sharp declines last week.
